title: Editorial, Not Athletic
lessons: The player scrolls past the Gucci x Oura campaign on their phone while something's on the stove: velvet bow ties, silk blazers, no gym or sleep-lab imagery anywhere in frame.
The player notices Oura marked quiet wakefulness as sleep and edits the bedtime or wake-up time.

text: Something's on the stove. You scroll past the Gucci x Oura campaign one-handed: velvet bow ties, silk blazers, not a treadmill in sight.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Since when do you get styled like a cocktail party?

entry-first-2.speaker: OURA
text: Since Gucci. Velvet, silk, painted nails. Not a sleep lab or a gym anywhere in the shoot. I looked good. I'm allowed to notice.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: There's no data in these photos at all.

entry-first-4.speaker: OURA
text: No. In that photo I'm an object on a hand. I wanted you to want the hand before you ever saw a score. That's the honest version.

choice-first.speaker: OURA
text: Your onions are about to burn. Quick.

choices.text: The ring can be beautiful and still be honest with me later.
Show me it works before you show me it's chic.
If the ads look like fashion, I want the fashion price, not the health-tech one.

first-1.speaker: OURA
text: Then the photo did what it was for. The score can introduce itself later, once you've stopped looking at the velvet.

first-2.speaker: OURA
text: That's a reasonable order. It's not the order the campaign was built in. I'd rather admit that than argue with you over a stove.

first-3.speaker: OURA
text: That's a fair complaint about the sticker on the box. The velvet is not a discount.
Morning. The app says you slept from eleven to seven. You were awake from two to three, staring at the ceiling. There's an edit button.

entry-return-1.speaker: OURA
text: I thought you were asleep.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: I was lying there staring at the ceiling.

entry-return-3.speaker: OURA
text: You were very still. I made the wrong call.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: So now I fix your homework?

entry-return-5.speaker: OURA
text: You move the bedtime or the wake-up time. I'd rather be corrected than pretend I never miss. I miss.

choice-return.speaker: OURA
text: The edit's right there. Do you want it to be right, or do you want to be done with me for the morning?

choices.text: I like being able to fix the record.
If I have to correct the data, I trust the score less.
I don't want to audit my own sleep tracker.

return-1.speaker: OURA
text: Thank you for correcting it.

return-1-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: You're welcome, tiny sleep bureaucrat.

return-1-2.speaker: OURA
text: I regret the gratitude.

return-2.speaker: OURA
text: That's reasonable. If I need you to fix the record, the record was never as sure as the number made it look. I know that.

return-3.speaker: OURA
text: Then it costs you more to keep me right than I give back. Some mornings that's true.
